title: Top Weekend Getaways from Bangalore for Nature, Adventure & Relaxation | Story | Hero Traveler
content:
Trek to Chembra Peak for stunning valley views, take a bamboo raft ride on Kuruva Island, or explore Edakkal Caves to witness ancient carvings. The best part? It’s far less commercialized than Ooty or Munnar.

Best time to visit: October to May Nearby attractions: Banasura Sagar Dam, Meenmutty Waterfalls

5. Kabini – For Wildlife and River Safaris [...] For nature lovers and photographers, Kabini offers a raw, wild beauty that few destinations can match. Located about 210 km from Bangalore, this former hunting reserve is now part of Nagarhole National Park — home to tigers, leopards, elephants, and exotic birds.

Go on a jeep safari or a boat safari on the Kabini River — both promise unforgettable sightings and serene landscapes. It’s an ideal choice for couples or families who want a peaceful, luxurious weekend close to nature. [...] When you think of a refreshing weekend away, Coorg is almost everyone’s first choice — and for good reason. Just 260 km from Bangalore, this hill station is wrapped in coffee estates, lush forests, and the soothing sound of rain.

You can spend your time exploring Abbey Falls, Raja’s Seat, and the Namdroling Monastery, or take on the Tadiandamol Trek, the highest peak in Coorg. Evenings are best spent sipping freshly brewed coffee while watching mist roll over the hills.

title: In Less Than 6 Hours From Bangalore, Travel To These Off-Beat Weekend Destinations. - Tripoto
content:
1.) You can take a leisurely stroll across Sim’s park that hosts exquisite species of plants sourced from around the world.

2.) Hike to Catherine Falls. It is a steep trek with broken steps and entwined roots, but the view of the tea gardens from the top of the falls is surreal.

3.) Take the vintage train in Coonoor which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The ticket is pocket-friendly and there are lots of Instagram-able backdrops on the way. [...] Image Credit: Blog

2.) Head to uninhabited Kuruva island for a private picnic, 950 acres of evergreen forest on the tributaries of east flowing river Kabani, far away from the city life. One can spot rare species of birds, orchids, and herbs here.

3.) Camp atop the Chembra Peak for an amazing experience. The climb up the is an exhilarating experience, as each stage in the climb unfolds great expanses of Wayanad and the view gets extensive and breath-taking as one goes up to its summit. [...] 3.) Revel in nature’s lap, surrounded by paddy fields at the Iruppu Falls. This is a 60-meter high waterfall with Rameshwara Temple on its banks.

Best Time To Go: November and January is the best time to spot wildlife in Kabini. July to October are the monsoon months when the entire land-mass dons a lush green blanket.
